g.text: MIT-Indoors vs NYU-Depth as object-graph corpora

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; fill: #6b6a63

g.text: MIT is 4.5x NYU's size and holds 83% of its vocabulary, yet every corpus lands within 0.53e-3 of the others — inside this backbone's ~0.0017 resolution.

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; fill: #6b6a63

g.text: Raw MIT − NYU is +0.53e-3 (t=+1.44, n.s.); size-matched it falls to +0.13e-3 (t=+0.62). What little advantage MIT has is corpus size, not corpus quality — which is the arm the size-matched

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; fill: #6b6a63

g.text: control exists to isolate. NYU also has the highest intrinsic encoder AUC and the lowest downstream score, the fourth instance in this study of intrinsic quality failing to predict recommendation.
